facts.statement: Uruguaysuchus was related to the genera Simosuchus and Malawisuchus.
facts.quote: It was related to Simosuchus and Malawisuchus.

facts.statement: In 1932, approximately seven individuals of small terrestrial crocodiles were discovered during a water well drilling in Guichón, Paysandú department, Uruguay.
facts.quote: En 1932, durante la perforación de un pozo de agua en la localidad de Guichón, departamento de Paysandú, Uruguay se descubrieron varios restos óseos pertenecientes a aproximadamente siete individuos de pequeños cocodrilos terrestres.

facts.statement: Carlos Rusconi described the new genus Uruguaysuchus and two new species, U. aznarezi and U. terrai, in 1933.
facts.quote: Carlos Rusconi en 1933 reconoce un nuevo género: Uruguaysuchus; y dos nuevas especies: U. aznarezi y U. terrai.

facts.statement: Uruguaysuchus remains the best-represented Mesozoic vertebrate in Uruguay.
facts.quote: Uruguaysuchus sigue siendo el vertebrado mesozoico mejor representado de Uruguay.

facts.statement: Uruguaysuchus is classified within the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
Uruguaysuchus belongs to the suborder Notosuchia.
Uruguaysuchus is the type genus of the family Uruguaysuchidae.
Uruguaysuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous in the Guichón Formation of Uruguay.
facts.quote: Uruguaysuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms from the Late Cretaceous Guichón Formation of Uruguay.

facts.statement: The time range for Uruguaysuchus is from the Cenomanian to the Santonian, between 100.5 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Santonian (100.5 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Uruguaysuchus was small to moderate in size, reaching an estimated length of 120 cm.
rejected.quote: It was of small to moderate size reaching an estimated length of 120 cm.
